world.title: South African police investigate death of 10th woman near Johannesburg
world.summary: South African police found a woman’s body on Sept. 26 near Mooifontein Cemetery in the Vusimusi section of Tembisa, east of Johannesburg. The discovery brought the number of women found dead in Ekurhuleni over roughly two months to 10. Police have not publicly identified the latest victim, and investigators are gatheri
world.content: South African police found a woman’s body on Sept. 26 near Mooifontein Cemetery in the Vusimusi section of Tembisa, east of Johannesburg. The discovery brought the number of women found dead in Ekurhuleni over roughly two months to 10. Police have not publicly identified the latest victim, and investigators are gathering evidence. A post-mortem is expected to establish the cause of death. Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni said similarities among some cases warrant investigation, but police have not established that the deaths are connected. He said investigators could not rule out a serial killer, while police are treating the killing of the ninth victim as an isolated case at this stage.

world.title: Ireland players back Israel fixtures in squad vote
world.summary: The Football Association of Ireland said the national team will play Israel in a UEFA Nations League match in Debrecen, Hungary, on Sunday, Sept. 27, after the squad voted by what the FAI called a “significant majority” to proceed. The return fixture, designated as Ireland’s home match, is scheduled for Oct. 4 in Backa
world.content: The Football Association of Ireland said the national team will play Israel in a UEFA Nations League match in Debrecen, Hungary, on Sunday, Sept. 27, after the squad voted by what the FAI called a “significant majority” to proceed. The return fixture, designated as Ireland’s home match, is scheduled for Oct. 4 in Backa Topola, Serbia, after security and disruption concerns prompted organizers to move it from Dublin. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad after expressing discomfort with the fixture. The vote followed calls in Ireland to boycott the matches because of Israel’s war in Gaza, as well as lengthy discussions among players, coaching staff and FAI officials.

world.title: Hamas chief dismisses Israeli election, outlines Gaza roadmap
world.summary: Hamas political leader Khalil al-Hayya said in a Saturday interview with Qatar’s Al-Araby that he expects Israel’s October election to bring no change for Palestinians, who he said have suffered under governments from all Israeli parties. He said Hamas agreed last October to a roadmap linking implementation of the Gaza
world.content: Hamas political leader Khalil al-Hayya said in a Saturday interview with Qatar’s Al-Araby that he expects Israel’s October election to bring no change for Palestinians, who he said have suffered under governments from all Israeli parties. He said Hamas agreed last October to a roadmap linking implementation of the Gaza ceasefire to the establishment of a Palestinian state, with Hamas’s weapons to be addressed as part of the overall package. Al-Hayya did not explicitly say Hamas would disarm. Al-Hayya also said Hamas was prepared to participate in Palestinian parliamentary elections as part of a national coalition and was ready to meet Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas. He warned that postponing the vote would interfere with internal reconciliation between Hamas and Fatah.

world.title: South African police hunt suspects after two township shootings
world.summary: At least 27 people were killed and 26 wounded in separate shootings in South Africa on Saturday night and early Sunday, Sept. 26-27. In Wedela, southwest of Johannesburg, gunmen killed 17 people and wounded 15 at a tavern. Police said they were seeking eight suspects, and the motive was unknown. In Lwandle, near Cape T
world.content: At least 27 people were killed and 26 wounded in separate shootings in South Africa on Saturday night and early Sunday, Sept. 26-27. In Wedela, southwest of Johannesburg, gunmen killed 17 people and wounded 15 at a tavern. Police said they were seeking eight suspects, and the motive was unknown. In Lwandle, near Cape Town, a separate attack at an entertainment venue killed 10 people and wounded 11, police said. The shootings followed a Sept. 23 attack at a house party near Durban that killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.

world.title: Russian strikes halt Ukraine’s largest steelmaker as attacks kill 16
world.summary: Russian and Ukrainian strikes killed at least 16 people in 24 hours, authorities on both sides said. Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks killed at least six people in Sumy, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk, including a 17-year-old girl. Russian officials reported deaths in Krasnodar and Belgorod, as well as in Russ
world.content: Russian and Ukrainian strikes killed at least 16 people in 24 hours, authorities on both sides said. Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks killed at least six people in Sumy, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk, including a 17-year-old girl. Russian officials reported deaths in Krasnodar and Belgorod, as well as in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Kyiv also came under repeated attacks, and Ukrainian officials said Russian forces struck residential areas and other civilian sites. ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine’s largest steel plant, halted production after four strikes in five weeks extensively damaged the facility; the company said it could no longer operate safely and sustainably. The latest strike cited by the company was on September 21. RT reported that production at the country’s three largest plants had halted. Ukraine also said it had struck the Ilsky oil refinery and a Russian defense-production plant.
world.image_alt: Russian strikes halt Ukraine’s largest steelmaker as attacks kill 16

world.title: Bangkok declares disaster as floods affect 52,000 households
world.summary: Bangkok declared a flood disaster across all 50 districts on Saturday after nearly 300 millimeters of rain fell over about 48 hours, flooding roads and homes and disrupting traffic. Thailand’s disaster agency reported two flood-related deaths in Chanthaburi province; RT also reported a death in Bangkok, citing the Thai
world.content: Bangkok declared a flood disaster across all 50 districts on Saturday after nearly 300 millimeters of rain fell over about 48 hours, flooding roads and homes and disrupting traffic. Thailand’s disaster agency reported two flood-related deaths in Chanthaburi province; RT also reported a death in Bangkok, citing the Thai newspaper Matichon. The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration said Sunday that rainfall had eased, but canal levels remained high. The governor warned that flooding was not over. Officials urged residents to stay home and those living near canals to move belongings upstairs. The army deployed relief teams, while schools and other sites were used as shelters.
world.image_alt: Bangkok declares disaster as floods affect 52,000 households

world.title: Athens blast kills six, including four American tourists
world.summary: An explosion on Friday morning, Sept. 25, caused a residential building to collapse in Athens’ historic Plaka district. By Saturday, rescuers had recovered six bodies: four U.S. citizens staying in a rental apartment and an elderly British man and Greek woman who lived in the building. Authorities had not formally rele
world.content: An explosion on Friday morning, Sept. 25, caused a residential building to collapse in Athens’ historic Plaka district. By Saturday, rescuers had recovered six bodies: four U.S. citizens staying in a rental apartment and an elderly British man and Greek woman who lived in the building. Authorities had not formally released the victims’ identities. Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said officials believed a major gas leak caused the blast, but investigators had not established its cause. The explosion damaged nearby buildings and vehicles, and authorities evacuated neighboring properties while the fire service’s criminal investigation unit examined the scene.
world.image_alt: Athens blast kills six, including four American tourists

world.title: US and China agree to AI incident hotline
world.summary: The United States and China agreed to establish a direct channel to communicate about artificial-intelligence-related incidents after President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met during Xi’s three-day state visit to Washington, Sept. 23-25. The governments also agreed to hold a dialogue on the technology
world.content: The United States and China agreed to establish a direct channel to communicate about artificial-intelligence-related incidents after President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met during Xi’s three-day state visit to Washington, Sept. 23-25. The governments also agreed to hold a dialogue on the technology’s risks and benefits, with another meeting due by November. The White House said the leaders agreed to use “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” for the technology. Neither government has explained what would qualify as an incident or how the channel would operate. Trump said the United States would not slow its AI efforts or share its advances with China.
world.image_alt: US and China agree to AI incident hotline

business.title: UK prime minister unveils 20% homebuyer loan scheme
business.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced “Your First Home,” a scheme for first-time buyers in England purchasing new-build homes. business.content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced “Your First Home,” a scheme for first-time buyers in England purchasing new-build homes. It offers an equity loan worth 20% of a property’s value, requires a minimum deposit of 2.5% and includes an initial interest-free period. The scheme targets buyers who have been unable to save a large deposit or lack financial support from their families. The government said the programme is also intended to encourage housebuilding. Further details are due in the October Budget.

business.title: Trump weighs diesel export ban as U.S. prices rise
business.summary: President Trump has supported considering a temporary ban on U.S. diesel exports, with officials reportedly exploring a 90-day restriction to increase domestic supply and lower prices before November’s congressional elections. U.S. diesel prices surpassed $6.50 per gallon, a record, on Sept. 22 as supply disruptions li
business.content: President Trump has supported considering a temporary ban on U.S. diesel exports, with officials reportedly exploring a 90-day restriction to increase domestic supply and lower prices before November’s congressional elections. U.S. diesel prices surpassed $6.50 per gallon, a record, on Sept. 22 as supply disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and attacks on Russian refineries tightened fuel markets. The proposal remains unsettled. Energy Secretary Chris Wright has warned that a full ban could disrupt U.S. refinery operations and raise prices for other fuels. He also asked oil companies to consider voluntary export cuts, though Danas reported that no major company had confirmed doing so. Separately, Senator Ted Cruz said the White House had assured refinery executives it would not ban diesel exports, Bloomberg reported.

business.content: A federal jury in San Diego ordered Apple to pay Taction Technology more than $5.7 billion after finding that the Taptic Engine in iPhones and Apple Watches infringed two Taction patents covering haptic technology. Taction alleged that Apple used its patented vibration technology without authorization. The jury did not find that Apple’s infringement was willful. Apple said the Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction’s technology and that it would appeal.

business.content: Work requirements for some Medicaid beneficiaries are scheduled to begin nationwide in January 2027 under President Donald Trump’s 2025 tax and policy law. Federal rules allow states to accept a person’s statement that a medical condition prevents them from working during the first year, but at least six states will require provider documentation from the start, while other states are considering similar requirements. The rules have also prompted disputes over how states should assess medical exemptions and administer the federal requirements.

business.content: Bitcoin traded around $84,000 near the end of the third quarter after reaching a weekly high of $87,363 and retreating. It had gained about 43.5% since early July, when it traded near $58,500, putting it on track for its strongest quarterly performance since 2017, when it rose about 80%. Its weekly gain was 3.6%, while spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded about $2.39 billion in net inflows from Sept. 21 to 25. Positive ETF flows and reduced uncertainty after the U.S. Federal Reserve’s September policy decision supported prices, while rising U.S. bond yields weighed on the crypto market. Bitcoin traded near $84,626.50 on Sunday, Sept. 27.

science.title: Super El Niño breaks Pacific temperature records, raises extreme-weather risks
science.summary: A strengthening El Niño has pushed equatorial Pacific sea-surface temperatures higher than during any previous recorded El Niño, and experts expect it to affect weather worldwide in the coming months. El Niño is a natural climate pattern that shifts tropical Pacific rainfall and can bring heat, drought and flooding. It
science.content: A strengthening El Niño has pushed equatorial Pacific sea-surface temperatures higher than during any previous recorded El Niño, and experts expect it to affect weather worldwide in the coming months. El Niño is a natural climate pattern that shifts tropical Pacific rainfall and can bring heat, drought and flooding. It occurs irregularly, typically every three to seven years. The current event follows the 2023–24 episode. Experts estimate that extreme heat associated with the event could contribute to 451,000 additional deaths between June 2026 and February 2027. The World Meteorological Organization has begun an unprecedented mobilization to prepare for extreme weather, Euronews reported. Climate scientist Mat Collins said El Niño and human-caused global heating are separate influences that can compound one another.
science.image_alt: Super El Niño breaks Pacific temperature records, raises extreme-weather risks

science.title: Psychology studies find appearance, worldview shape judgments
science.summary: Two psychology studies published in separate journals examined how social cues and beliefs affect judgments of other people. In a small study in the International Journal of Psychophysiology, participants reported greater empathy for attractive people described as criminals than for less attractive people. Moral judgme
science.content: Two psychology studies published in separate journals examined how social cues and beliefs affect judgments of other people. In a small study in the International Journal of Psychophysiology, participants reported greater empathy for attractive people described as criminals than for less attractive people. Moral judgments dominated self-reported pity, while attractiveness had a subtler effect on measures of brain activity. A separate series of four studies, published in the Journal of Individual Differences, found that people who view the world as dangerous tend to overestimate specific threats and rate neutral faces as less trustworthy and more aggressive.

science.title: Astronomers detect radio emissions from exoplanet Beta Pictoris b
science.summary: A team led by Harvard-Smithsonian astrophysicist Kevin Ortiz Ceballos says it detected radio emissions directly from the exoplanet Beta Pictoris b using South Africa’s MeerKAT radio telescope. The finding, described in a paper that has not yet been peer reviewed, would be the first direct detection of radio signals fro
science.content: A team led by Harvard-Smithsonian astrophysicist Kevin Ortiz Ceballos says it detected radio emissions directly from the exoplanet Beta Pictoris b using South Africa’s MeerKAT radio telescope. The finding, described in a paper that has not yet been peer reviewed, would be the first direct detection of radio signals from an exoplanet. Beta Pictoris b is a gas giant about 64 light-years from Earth with a mass about 12 times Jupiter’s. Researchers say natural auroras most likely produce its radio emissions.

science.title: Creatine studies examine effects with and without exercise
science.summary: A study of 64 healthy adults ages 45 to 65 found that creatine supplementation was associated with gains in strength and lean tissue, including among participants who did not follow a structured exercise program. In the exercise-and-weight-loss arm, participants taking creatine gained nearly three pounds of lean tissue
science.content: A study of 64 healthy adults ages 45 to 65 found that creatine supplementation was associated with gains in strength and lean tissue, including among participants who did not follow a structured exercise program. In the exercise-and-weight-loss arm, participants taking creatine gained nearly three pounds of lean tissue and reduced fat mass over 12 weeks, while placebo participants showed little change in lean tissue. A separate Australian trial followed 63 healthy adults ages 18 to 50 with limited regular-training experience. Participants completed a 12-week resistance-training program three times a week, and the trial tested five grams of creatine daily. Because the studies enrolled different populations and used different exercise conditions, they did not directly replicate one another.
science.image_alt: Creatine studies examine effects with and without exercise

science.title: Researchers test atmosphere-breathing engine for very-low-orbit satellites
science.summary: A plasma-engine concept explored by Francesco Romano during his PhD research at the University of Stuttgart would collect atmospheric molecules and use them as propellant, potentially eliminating the need to carry conventional fuel. Laboratory tests and modeling show promise, but the engine has not been demonstrated on
science.content: A plasma-engine concept explored by Francesco Romano during his PhD research at the University of Stuttgart would collect atmospheric molecules and use them as propellant, potentially eliminating the need to carry conventional fuel. Laboratory tests and modeling show promise, but the engine has not been demonstrated on a satellite mission. The proposed system targets very low Earth orbit, which the research article defines as roughly 100 to 450 kilometers above Earth. Satellites at those altitudes experience enough atmospheric drag to require near-continuous thrust to maintain orbit.
science.image_alt: Researchers test atmosphere-breathing engine for very-low-orbit satellites

science.content: California has improved its ability to capture and store rainwater after drought, but a strong El Niño could bring more precipitation than the state can retain, sending some runoff into the Pacific, The New York Times reported. In Marin County, workers are staging pumps, sandbags and other storm supplies ahead of possible winter storms as several king tides approach.

sports.content: England beat New Zealand 26-19 at Allianz Stadium on September 26 after Zoe Harrison intercepted a pass and scored on the final play to break a 19-19 tie. Harrison had missed a penalty moments earlier. A crowd of 59,871 watched the WXV Global Series test. The win extended England’s unbeaten run to 41 Tests after England's record 39-match winning streak ended in a 26-26 draw against Canada the previous week. New Zealand, the last team to beat England—in the 2022 World Cup final—suffered its first loss under head coach Whitney Hansen.

sports.content: No. 17 Iowa beat No. 18 Michigan 20-19 in Ann Arbor on Sept. 26 in the Big Ten opener when Hank Brown threw a 16-yard touchdown pass to Reece Vander Zee on the final play. Vander Zee kept both feet in bounds with two seconds left, giving the Hawkeyes a road victory. Michigan led for more than 40 minutes. The result moved Iowa to 4-0 overall and 1-0 in conference play, while Michigan fell to 3-1 and 0-1 in the Big Ten.

sports.content: Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points to beat Taylor Fritz 6-3, 4-6, 13-11 on Saturday, giving Team Europe a 7-5 lead over Team World after the second day of the Laver Cup at London’s O2 Arena. Alcaraz’s victory followed Team World taking the lead through Alex de Minaur’s comeback win over Alexander Zverev and Learner Tien’s victory against Flavio Cobolli. Casper Ruud and Zverev then closed the day by defeating Alexander Bublik and Brandon Nakashima in doubles. Sunday, September 27, is the tournament’s final day.

sports.content: The International team holds a 10.5–7.5 lead over the United States heading into Sunday’s 12 singles matches at Medinah Country Club in Illinois. sports.title: USMNT begin 2030 cycle with 4-1 win over Peru
sports.summary: The United States opened its 2030 World Cup cycle with a 4-1 friendly win over Peru at Orlando’s Inter&Co Stadium on September 26, the team’s first match since its 2026 World Cup elimination. Justin Ellis scored in the fourth minute from a Gio Reyna free kick; Gianluca Lapadula equalized for Peru in the 15th, before Ma
sports.content: The United States opened its 2030 World Cup cycle with a 4-1 friendly win over Peru at Orlando’s Inter&Co Stadium on September 26, the team’s first match since its 2026 World Cup elimination. Justin Ellis scored in the fourth minute from a Gio Reyna free kick; Gianluca Lapadula equalized for Peru in the 15th, before Malik Tillman converted a second-half penalty, Julian Hall scored in the 72nd minute and Sebastian Berhalter added a goal in the 90th. Coach Mauricio Pochettino gave 11 players their senior international debuts, including 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan, who started for the United States. Ellis and Hall also scored on their debuts. The match was the first in the United States’ four-year buildup to the 2030 World Cup.
sports.image_alt: USMNT begin 2030 cycle with 4-1 win over Peru

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu wi
sports.content: The Republic of Ireland will play Israel in their UEFA Nations League fixture in Debrecen, Hungary, on Sunday, September 27, after players held several hours of discussions and voted by what Football Association of Ireland chief executive David Courell called a “significant majority” to play. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad after telling coach Heimir Hallgrimsson he was uncomfortable taking part. The squad plans to wear black armbands in memory of people killed in the Gaza conflict and skip parts of the pre-match ceremony. Players will donate their Israel-match fees to charity, while the FAI will donate proceeds from the Austria fixture. Ireland and Israel are also scheduled to meet again on October 4 in Backa Topola, Serbia.

sports.title: Fury puts chance of December Joshua fight at 1%
sports.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua’s long-awaited heavyweight bout was announced for Cardiff’s Principality Stadium on December 11, with a global Netflix broadcast. Within days, the event’s status became uncertain over a dispute between Joshua’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, and the other organizers about promoter Dana White’s inv
sports.content: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua’s long-awaited heavyweight bout was announced for Cardiff’s Principality Stadium on December 11, with a global Netflix broadcast. Within days, the event’s status became uncertain over a dispute between Joshua’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, and the other organizers about promoter Dana White’s involvement. Fury said Sunday that he believed the fight had a 1% chance of going ahead, while promoter Frank Warren said he expected it to happen because Saudi backers were financing it. The fight remains scheduled for December, but the articles report no final resolution to the promotional dispute.
sports.image_alt: Fury puts chance of December Joshua fight at 1%
